existing_terminology:
Health service is named "Speech and Language Therapy" at the Child Development Centre
Schools work from "special educational needs"; nearest label is "communication" impairment

existing_identificationCriteria:
Impairment must be long-term and require individualized accommodation
Child development centres under the Ministry of Health diagnose and assess

existing_referralPathway:
Referral into the psychology service is via any public or private clinic or hospital
Its clinical psychology unit takes referrals from hospitals and private clinics in Brunei
Its community psychology division takes referrals from government health centres and schools
Age gate: its children team at the Kiarong Child Development Centre serves ages 3 to 11
existing_serviceModel:
Health-sector model: the Child Development Centre at Kiarong is the paediatric hub
CDC pairs speech and language therapy with audiology, OT, physio and psychology
Therapists must hold AHPCBD registration; the Act took effect on 1 July 2017

2007 Compulsory Education Order ensures all children get at least 9 years of education

docLinks.label: Parami General Hospital, Yangon — 'Speech & Language Therapy Services' department page
UNESCO GEM Report PEER country profile, Myanmar — Inclusion (page states 'Validated by the country: No'; last modified Wed, 28/07/2021)

existing_terminology:
Leading private clinic's working label is "Expressive Receptive Language Disorder"
That is the pre-CATALISE term; DLD does not appear in any source read
No speech or language category in the 2014 National Education Law's list of special needs
Statutory groups are visually impaired, hearing impaired, mentally disabled, diverse learners
existing_identificationCriteria:
Evidence is a private hospital's service page, not a state criterion
A children's speech and language therapy team assesses and diagnoses
existing_multilingualProvision:
Rules found cover the language of schooling, not the language of assessment
Instruction is generally in English or Myanmar, under the 2014 education law
An ethnic language may be used as a medium of instruction at basic education level
A Department of Myanmar Nationalities' Languages promotes ethnic languages and local curricula
existing_referralPathway: Not established from the sources consulted. The UNESCO PEER profile for Myanmar records that individual education plans and referral systems based on learning assessment are not in place, and that limited knowledge of needs assessment has been reported for teachers in regular schools and other personnel. The only service description found is a private Yangon hospital's own department page, which sets out no route by which a child reaches it and no gate on who may come. Searched: the PEER Myanmar inclusion profile and the Parami General Hospital speech and language therapy page.
existing_serviceModel:
All service evidence is one private hospital's own page plus a 2021 UNESCO profile
Private, fee-charging clinic in Yangon describes itself as the first such centre in Myanmar
No public speech and language therapy service was found in any ministry source
Schools have no IEPs or referral systems in place; NGOs run the disability teacher training
existing_legalEntitlement:
2015 Rights of Persons with Disabilities Law, adopted after Myanmar ratified the CRPD in 2011
Free and compulsory education on a proximity principle, in all types of education institution
Enrolment may not be refused for impairment, but subject-requirement exceptions are allowed
Duty sits with the National Committee on disability rights and the Ministry of Education
existing_workforce:
Evidence is one private hospital's own page in Yangon, not a register or a count
The service calls itself the first and foremost centre of its kind in Myanmar
One named speech-language pathologist consults alongside a speech and language therapist

docLinks.label: UNESCO GEM Report, Profiles Enhancing Education Reviews (PEER), Turkmenistan: Inclusion

existing_terminology:
"Speech disorders" is a standing placement category, not a defined diagnosis
Medico-pedagogical commissions identify speech disorders and refer to special institutions
PEER: "An explicit definition of special education needs has not been found"
existing_identificationCriteria: Not established from the sources consulted. The UNESCO PEER profile states that an explicit definition of special education needs has not been found. It records medico-pedagogical commissions identifying children with speech disorders and referring them to specialized institutions, but states no evidence requirement, no threshold and no exclusion that those commissions apply.
existing_referralPathway:
Medico-pedagogical commissions identify speech disorders and refer to institutions
Staffed by special teachers, psychologists, speech therapists and defectologists
The same commissions transfer children between specialised institutions
PEER records that parents are not required to be consulted
existing_serviceModel:
Segregated preschool institutions exist for children with speech disorders
Remedial preschools, classes and groups are established by type of disability
Speech is a distinct type beside mental, physical, visual and hearing
existing_legalEntitlement:
PEER: the Law on Education embraces inclusive education for children with disabilities
The 2014 child rights law commits the state to regular education, inclusive in approach
Special schools are kept for children who cannot attend regular schools for health reasons
The 2008 Constitution enshrines the right to education and free public education
existing_workforce:
The 2016 quality policy aims to revise pre-service and in-service teacher curricula
The ministry of education must improve the professional development of education personnel
Teachers deployed to remote villages get a salary benefit (Law on Education, art. 45.3)

docLinks.label: UNESCO GEM Report, Profiles Enhancing Education Reviews (PEER), Mauritania: Inclusion

existing_terminology:
The concept of special educational needs is said to concern disability
No speech or language category; 'speech' occurs 0 times in the profile
No definition of inclusive education has been adopted
existing_identificationCriteria:
Mauritania has adopted no definition of inclusive education
The one condition-based rule is exclusion, not identification: Act 5-023 of 1975 art 9
A regional director decides, after consulting the Council of Teachers
Ground: a mental or physical condition incompatible with schoolwork, on a medical certificate
existing_referralPathway:
Children whose disability bars mainstream schooling are accommodated at the CFPSESH centre
Two buses run by the social affairs ministry carry children with disabilities to that centre
For street children a separate protection centre does identification, referral and reception
existing_serviceModel:
No speech or language therapy service is named in the profile
A centre for training and social advancement of children with disabilities
An educational complex for people with learning disabilities in Sebkha
existing_legalEntitlement:
Source describes special-needs provision generally, never language disorder
The Constitution does not enshrine a right to education, only equality before the law
Act 054-2001 art 10 fines a guardian who refuses without good reason to enrol a child
The 2011-2020 sector programme has no national inclusive or special education strategy
existing_workforce:
PEER records no national policy on specialist teacher training
The national disability council aspires to add a special education module at the teacher college
The state disability centre reports a shortage of professional trainers and specialist teachers

existing_identificationCriteria:

Health practitioners notify a child's disability to parents under Education Act Art. 31
With parent consent, notice passes to director of medical services and the principal
Many children go unidentified: parental resistance, insufficient resources and equipment
existing_assessments:
Source describes special-needs provision generally, never language disorder
2017 Inclusive Education Policy and Guidelines cover screening, referral and assessment
Delivered through teacher training and assistance programmes defining roles
2008-13 strategic plan prioritised training in disability assessment
existing_referralPathway:
A multi-disciplinary approach using health, education and other professionals
The policy seeks a memorandum between Education and Health on shared personnel
existing_serviceModel:
No speech and language service is named in any cited Nauru source
'speech' returns 0 hits in the Act, the inclusive education policy and the PDF review

Communication difficulties appear only as a sub-item under Intellectual needs
existing_legalEntitlement:

The Minister must establish a special education centre — mandatory, unlike Kiribati
existing_workforce:

existing_outcomesEvidence:

docLinks.label: Landsbesluit logopedische hulp, Afkondigingsblad van Aruba 2023 no. 36

existing_terminology:
Decree names stoornissen in het spreken of leren spreken en in het gebruiken van de taal
Decree names taalontwikkelingsstoornissen once, in a dialect/anderstaligheid exclusion
existing_identificationCriteria:
Aim must be herstellen, verbeteren or onderhouden of gehoor-, stem- of spraakorganen
Opheffen van stoornissen in het spreken of leren spreken also qualifies
Nothing judged onnodig kostbaar, onnodig gecompliceerd or niet doelmatig is approved
Dyslexie carries no aanspraak under the decree
existing_multilingualProvision: No AZV cover for a taalontwikkelingsstoornis tied to dialect or anderstaligheid
existing_referralPathway:
Referral is by the huisarts or medisch specialist already treating the insured
Toestemming is requested in writing, with a copy of the verwijzing attached
The verwijzing carries the diagnostic data thought relevant for the logopedist
A refusal is notified to the verwijzende arts as well as the insured
existing_serviceModel:
Speciaal onderwijs school types are MLK, ZMLK and dove en slechthorende kinderen
Logopedische hulp became an AZV entitlement by landsbesluit of 29 August 2023
Toestemming is expressed in zittingen, at most fifteen, and ten further in bijzondere gevallen
Aanspraak holds only so far as the Uitvoeringsorgaan has given toestemming
existing_legalEntitlement:
A verzekerde has aanspraak op behandeling door een logopedist under the AZV
The decree rests on articles 13a and 22 of the Landsverordening AZV
An eigen bijdrage of 10 percent of the tariff falls on the verzekerde
existing_funding:
The Uitvoeringsorgaan may waive the eigen bijdrage where a verzekerde's income makes it unfair
The toestemming decision goes to the contractant or contracting institution as well
